rationale: Lycopolitan ⲍⲗⲗⲟ = Sahidic ϩⲗⲗⲟ 'old man, elder.' Standard ⲍ-for-ϩ Lyc. orthographic feature. Used here as the central figure of this section — the humble elderly disciple at whom the noble assembly laughs.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲛⲁϩⲣⲛ̄ⲧⲏⲩⲧⲛ̄ 'before/in the presence of you (pl.).' Standard Coptic compound preposition with 2pl suffix in Lyc. dialect. Recurs both lines 10 and 12 of this page.

Qualitative of an ⲁⲃⲁⲗ-compound verb of emergence; possibly Lyc. reflex of ϣⲱⲗ in extended sense 'go forth, emanate' or related to ϣⲗⲁ 'flame, blaze.' Used in l.24 of the beauty of uprightness emerging from the disciple. Confidence low.
Greek loanword κοινωνέω 'have fellowship with, partake.' Standard NT/early Christian register. Used in the Matthew 18 citation for fellowship with 'one of the little faithful ones.'

ⲛⲓⲕⲟⲩⲓ̄ 'the little ones' + ⲙⲡⲓⲥⲧⲟⲥ 'of-the-faithful' (Greek loanword πιστός). Manichaean adaptation of Matthew 18's μικροί ('little ones') by adding the πιστός qualifier — the humble elect/faithful within the community.
